name: Danelaw
alt: Kingdom of York (as its last remnant)

predecessors.name: Viking settlements
predecessors.text: East Anglia, the East Midlands and Yorkshire, as Cliopatria's Danelaw shape of 878

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Mercia
predecessors.text: the eastern Midlands that Cliopatria adds in 880

successors.name: Kingdom of England
successors.text: the York remnant: Yorkshire between the Humber and the Tees

ledger.x: 878: after Edington the Danes hold East Anglia, the East Midlands and Yorkshire: the Danelaw.
880: Cliopatria's Danelaw grows by 43 cells of the Midlands (10.9 thousand km2, 1.6-0.1 W, 51.6-53.3 N).
915: Edward's reconquest of the Danelaw begins in earnest.
915: Edward occupies Bedford and builds a fort on the south bank of the Great Ouse.
917: the Danes of Northampton, Cambridge and East Anglia submit to Edward.
917: Æthelflæd, Lady of the Mercians, takes Derby.
early 918: Leicester submits to Æthelflæd 'without a fight'.
918: Stamford surrenders to Edward and Nottingham follows; the Chronicle for 918 states 'All the people who had settled in Mercia, both Danish and English, submitted to him.'
918: the Danelaw south of the Humber is Edward's.
939: York takes Olaf Guthfrithson as king.
947: Eric Bloodaxe takes York and the contest with Eadred begins.
954: Eric is killed at Stainmore and the contest ends.
954: the Danelaw ends as a state.

wars.name: Battle of Edington
wars.outcome: Alfred defeats Guthrum at Edington; the Treaty of Wedmore follows and the Danes keep East Anglia and the north.

wars.name: Battle of Tettenhall
wars.outcome: A Mercian and West Saxon force dealt a 'decisive defeat' to an invading Northumbrian army; the Viking kings Eowils and Halfdan II were killed 'at Tettenhall on 5 August 910' (York page).

wars.name: Edward the Elder's and Æthelflæd's reconquest of the Danelaw
wars.outcome: By the end of 918 the Danes of Bedford, Northampton, Cambridge, East Anglia, Derby, Leicester, Stamford and Nottingham had submitted; only York stayed Danish (Norse from 919).

wars.name: Æthelstan's conquest of York
wars.outcome: Æthelstan 'conquered the last remaining Viking kingdom, York' in 927.

wars.name: Olaf Guthfrithson's recovery of York
wars.outcome: York chooses Olaf Guthfrithson in 939; he invades Mercia and East Anglia in 941; Eadmund expels the Viking leaders from Northumbria in 944.

wars.name: Eric Bloodaxe and Eadred
wars.outcome: Eric rules at York in 947, is driven out in 948, rules again 952-954 and is killed at Stainmore; Eadred then holds Northumbria.

certainty.note: No boundary is dated; the treaty line is placed only 'between 878 and Guthrum's death in 890'.
The treaty of Alfred and Guthrum fixes the frontier up the Thames and the Lea to Bedford and up the Ouse to Watling Street; the date of the line is uncertain (878-890).
The frontier moves with each fortress taken (915-918) and the York remnant has no dated boundary beyond the Tees and the Humber.
